video_title: Lou Will - 76ers are DANGEROUS! LeBron UNLOCKS Tyrese Maxey, Jaylen Brown MOST Impactful NBA Player?

quotes.speaker: Chandler Parsons
quotes.summary_phrase: Chandler Parsons on the Sixers' versatility and offensive potential
quotes.excerpt: we saw the versatility, we saw their offensive way they want to play
quotes.quote: It was one game but all the questions that I know I had got answered last night. We saw the versatility, we saw their offensive way they want to play, how they want to get stops and get out in transition, let Tyrese Maxey do what he does best. We saw the defensive versatility of LeBron James at 42 years old last night, it really blew my mind. You saw him guard one through five, you saw him man-handle Karl-Anthony Towns on certain possessions and get the break going to where LeBron can be himself, to where Jaylen Brown is best. I think just seeing him fully buy into what this team needs from him on the defensive end makes this team's offense that much better. He is a man of many hats, he has done this before, he is one of the more versatile players to ever play this game. He is okay with not having 30, 35 point scoring nights sometimes because he can do all the little things which he did last night.

quotes.speaker: DeMarcus Cousins
quotes.summary_phrase: DeMarcus Cousins on the Sixers' unselfish team identity
quotes.excerpt: This is a team that's about winning a championship at the end of the year
quotes.quote: I was impressed and I was more so concerned with how everybody would have the opportunity with the basketball and I think they did a great job of showing that balance, showing that unselfishness early, setting the tone early for a very long season. But I think the message is very clear: This is a team that's about winning a championship at the end of the year and it's obvious they don't really care whose night it is to shine. I like how they allow Tyrese Maxey to play, kind of be that open court firecracker type of player to where he's playing super fast, open and free. I think that's him playing as the best version of himself. Jaylen Brown being that kind of point-forward type of position and honestly, even when it goes down to Joel Embiid and Jaylen Brown, these guys were actually slowing down the game and just looking for the right read and the right play.

quotes.speaker: Lou Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: Lou Williams on LeBron James' role as a Swiss Army knife
quotes.excerpt: He was actually the Swiss Army knife. He was a guy that could go out and do a myriad of things
quotes.quote: We talk about LeBron, we've heard guys before say, 'I'm going to go to a team and I'm going to be the Swiss Army knife.' He was actually the Swiss Army knife. He was a guy that could go out and do a myriad of things for this group. I saw him play the five at some points, he was flashing to the middle of the court, finding open guys. He was in the dunker, he was initiating the break. Defensively, sometimes he likes to take chances and kind of play free safety back there and go double or go do things that he feels is necessary for the defense. He has the personnel around him that was covering a lot of holes when these guys were scrambling around. That made them a dangerous defensive team to me. More than anything, I was really impressed with LeBron, the way that he was able to fit in.

quotes.speaker: Lou Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: Lou Williams on how LeBron James unlocks Tyrese Maxey's scoring
quotes.excerpt: It opens up scoring lanes. That's one of the things that I noticed more than anything
quotes.quote: It opens up scoring lanes. That's one of the things that I noticed more than anything. He has the freedom to get to the rim whenever he wants to. He has the freedom to shoot the ball deep whenever he wants to. He has so many weapons around him, you can't really key in on him. The couple times that the Knicks did try to get the ball out of his hands and double, it didn't go their way. They had LeBron James in the middle of the floor playmaking. That makes this team dangerous once you realize that you can't trap Tyrese Maxey. You can't do those things, that's going to open up everything. Think about how many quick and easy buckets he was able to get out in transition by the ball being outletted to him and him catching it at half court with the defense already on their heels. I think this is going to unlock a different level of Tyrese Maxey that we've seen already, but I think it's going to put it on steroids with this group.

quotes.speaker: Chandler Parsons
quotes.summary_phrase: Chandler Parsons on the Sixers' depth and rotation flexibility
quotes.excerpt: I know depth is kind of early on the flaw of this team, but I saw plenty of depth
quotes.quote: We even saw game on the line last night where they go to a two-man game with Tyrese Maxey and with Joel Embiid, just a high pick-and-roll and then on the back side, you have Jaylen Brown and LeBron James and you have LeBron in the dunker and like you said, Kentavious Caldwell-Pope was making shots last night. Anthony Davis we know is just a bucket off the bench. Dean Wade didn't play, he's going to get some valuable minutes on that bench. So I know depth is kind of early on the flaw of this team, but I saw plenty of depth last night and they still got another guy that's going to play 20-25 minutes in Dean Wade who's going to play. Now, they're going to miss time, Joel Embiid is going to miss games, LeBron James is not going to play 82 games, so who's going to step up and get that production? That's where Tyrese Maxey's youth comes from. Jaylen Brown is still pretty young. LeBron James is very young. These guys are more than capable of filling those holes when these older experienced guys go down to not play every game.

quotes.speaker: DeMarcus Cousins
quotes.summary_phrase: DeMarcus Cousins on Tyrese Maxey's potential for a breakout season
quotes.excerpt: I think this can be one of those years where he can make that jump
quotes.quote: I'm excited for Tyrese Maxey individually. I think this can be one of those years where he can make that jump to that Kyrie Irving tier type of player. The reason I say that, we've seen the history of LeBron and what he can do with those explosive combo guard type of players. I think Tyrese Maxey fits that same type role. The fact that it's so many weapons around him, it obviously is going to open up the floor for him to play a fast and free type of style of play, which I think is great for him. But I just don't want to ignore the fact that LeBron does have a history of this and for the most part, those guys that have been in those positions, the Kyries, the Dwyane Wades, and obviously those are elite level players in this league and I think Tyrese has that type of potential.

quotes.speaker: DeMarcus Cousins
quotes.summary_phrase: DeMarcus Cousins on the difficulty of picking the most impactful player
quotes.excerpt: It's hard to sit there and say that he's not one of the most impactful
quotes.quote: I mean that's such a tough question because they have so much talent. Obviously Joel Embiid healthy, locked in, one of the best players in his league, top 10 player in his league in my opinion. So obviously he'll always have some form of an impact on the game, but when you think about Joel Embiid when he's healthy and you know what he's capable of, it's hard to sit there and say that he's not one of the most impactful. Even with Tyrese Maxey at this young age and he's still continuing to grow and figure out who he is in his league, he has a huge impact on his team. So it's hard to just single out any single person as far as the most impactful. But even LeBron in this form that he's in, like we said, quarterback on offense, safety on defense, that's a huge impact for any team in the league. So it's hard to just single out one guy.

quotes.speaker: Chandler Parsons
quotes.summary_phrase: Chandler Parsons on the Sixers' deep roster and versatility
quotes.excerpt: He guarded one through five and he's the fourth guy we're talking about on this team
quotes.quote: The beauty of this team too, you don't have to, right? Like we said, any given night can be someone's offensively night. And we talked about LeBron James guarding KAT. Jaylen Brown guarded Jalen Brunson. So this guy's versatility defensively, he guarded one through five and he's the fourth guy we're talking about on this team. That's just how star-loaded they are. So again, for 82 different games, we could have a different headline. There's going to be LeBron James come 30, 40 point games and he's going to be the talking point. Then the bench is going to go off for 40, 50 points in a game and we're going to talk about them. That is the balance and the versatility of this team and the beauty of this team.

quotes.speaker: Lou Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: Lou Williams on the Sixers' half-court execution and lack of bailouts
quotes.excerpt: It was Maxey in the open floor, but in half court, it was no bailouts for the Knicks
quotes.quote: It was Tyrese Maxey in the open floor, but in half court, it was no bailouts for the Knicks. They were putting Joel Embiid right in the post against Jalen Brunson, making them come over double and we're going to pick apart whatever y'all want to do on the defensive end. But they didn't bail out the Knicks not one time. Maybe Joel Embiid a couple times on some early threes, but we know that's the way that he plays, but other than that, they didn't bail the Knicks out at all. And if that was the measuring stick for how this Sixers team was going to play against the rest of the Eastern Conference, as well as the league, they put a lot of teams on notice.
